hints.title: Parity State Decomposition
hints.text: Track counts of valid non-empty subsequences ending in an even number versus an odd number.

hints.title: Alternating Extension Transition
hints.text: An incoming even number extends all previously formed odd subsequences plus starts a new singleton.

hints.title: Combined Subsequence Total
hints.text: Sum the even and odd ending counts modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def countStableSubsequences(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        # A subsequence is stable if adjacent elements alternate parities
        # dp0: ends with even, dp1: ends with odd
        dp0, dp1 = 0, 0
        
        for x in nums:
            if x % 2 == 0:
                # Even number can extend any odd subsequence, or start a new subsequence
                dp0 = (dp0 + dp1 + 1) % MOD
            else:
                # Odd number can extend any even subsequence, or start a new subsequence
                dp1 = (dp1 + dp0 + 1) % MOD
                
        return (dp0 + dp1) % MOD
```

complexity.notes: Single pass DP maintaining two scalar parity counts.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all 2^N subsequences takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Uses two scalar variables for O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use 2-state parity transitions to count alternating subsequences.
